Question: A large rectangle is partitioned into four rectangles by two segments parallel to its sides. The areas of three of the resulting rectangles are shown. What is the area of the fourth rectangle? \[\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 6 & 14\\ \hline \text{?} & 35\\ \hline\end{array}\]
Solution:
The two rectangles in the right column have the same width. Since rectangle area equals width times height, their area ratio equals their height ratio. Thus the bottom row is
\[
\frac{35}{14}=\frac52
\]
times as tall as the top row.

The same two row heights occur in the left column, whose two rectangles also share a width. Its bottom area is therefore \(5/2\) times its top area:
\[
6\cdot\frac52=\boxed{15}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{B}\).
